sections.html:
Doral is a Miami-Dade city of roughly 15 square miles, home to approximately 81,182 residents and to more than 100,000 jobs. Its closeness to Miami International Airport keeps people looking for housing. Since you are in Miami-Dade, the county's own deed tax rate applies, and the county appraiser and tax collector handle your assessment and bill.

Plenty of Doral homes belong to a condominium, townhome or homeowners association, and the association can set the pace of a sale more than any buyer does.

  • Listing makes sense when you can sit through showings and wait on a buyer's loan.
  • An as-is cash sale fits a firm move date, a repair bill or a tax deadline.
  • Whichever you choose, reach out to the association first about transfer fees, estoppel letters and approvals.

Four edges frame the city: the Ronald Reagan Turnpike to the west, the Town of Medley to the north, the Palmetto Expressway to the east and the City of Sweetwater to the south. The airport is about a mile off and Downtown Miami about twelve miles. Commuters touring your house will care about that highway access, so say so.

The first neighborhoods, Doral Estates and then Doral Park, went up in the early 1980s. Newer building later spread to Downtown Doral, City Place Doral and Midtown Doral, where many units sit inside condominium or townhome associations. That arrangement changes what a closing looks like. A county building moratorium from 1983 to 1985 protected the well fields, and construction picked up sharply once it ended, so houses in a given neighborhood often share an age.

Ask the association for its estoppel letter early, since it shows what you owe and any fees due at transfer. Missing that letter is a common reason a closing slips by a week. Find out your association's transfer rules before you take an offer. If a board must vote, the buyer waits, and days can pile onto a closing that was supposed to be fast.

No other Florida county uses Miami-Dade's formula: 60 cents on each $100 of price, with a 45 cents per $100 surtax on top. A deed that moves only a single-family dwelling escapes the surtax. The wording stops at single-family homes, so a condo or townhome seller should ask the closing agent how the surtax is handled.

All parties on the deed can be held liable, regardless of which side the contract names as the payer. The clerk collects at recording. Recording itself costs extra under section 28.24, with a first-page amount, a lower amount for each additional page and per-page add-ons.

November brings the bill, with a 4 percent early-payment discount that shrinks to 1 percent by February. April 1 is the day an unpaid bill turns delinquent, and tax certificates on those accounts are offered by June 1.

  • A TRIM notice from the property appraiser arrives each August. To contest value, file a petition with the clerk within 25 days of that notice.
  • Form DR-501, the homestead application, is due March 1.
  • The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser's exemptions page explains exemptions, assessment reductions and land use classifications.

Ask the Miami-Dade Tax Collector for a payoff figure before you close. Also change your mailing address, or the next November bill may go to an empty house.

sections.h2: Weighing a quick sale against listing
sections.html:
Judge each option on net proceeds, speed and how sure the close is. A listing means showings plus a buyer who needs a loan. A cash buyer drops the loan, but association approval, stamp costs and the closing date still need answers. A simple order of work helps:

  1. Request a payoff statement from your mortgage lender.
  2. If an HOA exists, ask for an estoppel letter.
  3. Confirm whether the tax bill is paid.
  4. Collect each buyer's terms in writing.

If foreclosure is pending, the clerk holds the public sale 20 to 35 days after final judgment, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait longer.

sections.h2: Checking the property record before you sell
sections.html:
Pull up your folio on the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser site. Owner names should match your deed, homestead should show if you live in the house, and the mailing address should be current.

  • Review the exemptions and assessment reductions listed for your parcel.
  • Ask the association whether any assessments are unpaid, because those can travel with the unit to closing.
  • If you did work on the house, check permits with Community Development.
  • Make sure the legal description on your deed lines up with the folio.

Note which municipality the record names, since that decides who answers permit and code questions. In Doral, that office is Community Development, one department alongside Public Works, Parks and Recreation, Finance and Police.

sections.h2: Carrying your Save Our Homes benefit
sections.html:
Buying another home in Florida? Portability can shift part of your capped benefit to the new homestead, as long as you set it up within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one. File Forms DR-501 and DR-501T with the property appraiser by March 1.

The state's cap chart, revised January 2026, prints 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. Renting the unit or moving out ends homestead, though section 196.061 lets a deployed servicemember rent without abandoning it. Condo owners heading to a different county should ask that county's appraiser how the benefit applies.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like from start to finish
sections.html: Nothing exotic happens in a cash sale; only the lender is missing. An offer arrives in writing and you accept it. A title company searches the record and picks a closing date. Meanwhile you collect payoff letters, association paperwork and your latest tax bill. At the table you sign the deed with two witnesses watching, the agent pays stamp tax, recording fees and any loan, and the remainder is yours. Offers differ in more than price, so line them up side by side and ask each buyer what happens if the title search turns up a surprise. Insist that the closing date and who pays which cost are written down, and never send money or sign over title early.

A tidy folder saves more time than any negotiating trick. Bring your recorded deed, the legal description, the latest mortgage statement or a request for a payoff, and records for work done on the house. Add association contact details, any open violation notices, and leases with deposit records if someone rents the unit. If the owner has died, the title company will want to see who has authority to sign for the estate. Having everything in one place lets the title search begin the day you accept an offer.

faqs.a: January 28, 2003, making it one of thirty-four municipalities in Miami-Dade County.
The city covers about 15 square miles and has approximately 81,182 residents.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: The county charges 60 cents per $100 and adds a 45 cents per $100 surtax. A document that transfers only a single-family dwelling does not owe the surtax.

faqs.q: When do Miami-Dade tax bills go delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The discount starts at 4 percent in November and falls to 1 percent in February.

faqs.q: Does Doral's building history matter to buyers?
faqs.a: It can. Building was frozen by the county from 1983 to 1985, and many neighborhoods began as Doral Estates and Doral Park, so nearby homes often share an age band.
